title: Window Functions
subtitle: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG, LEAD, and PARTITION BY
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: GROUP BY collapses rows — you can't see individual rows alongside their group aggregate. You can't rank items within a group without complex subqueries. You can't compare a row to the previous row.
whyItExists.solution: Window functions compute across a 'window' of related rows without collapsing them. Each row keeps its identity but gains computed values from its neighbors — rank, running total, previous value.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Ranking items per group. Running totals. Moving averages. Comparing a row to the previous/next row. Percentiles. Leaderboards.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Window functions are computed after GROUP BY — if you need one aggregate per group and no row-level detail, GROUP BY is simpler.

explainModes.beginner: Imagine a leaderboard. GROUP BY COUNT(*) tells you 'user 1 has 3 orders' — but collapses to one row. A window function lets you see all orders AND add a rank column showing '1st, 2nd, 3rd most expensive' — keeping all rows intact.
explainModes.simple: func() OVER (PARTITION BY col ORDER BY col2). PARTITION BY divides rows into groups (like GROUP BY but doesn't collapse). ORDER BY within OVER determines order within the window. ROW_NUMBER() — 1,2,3 per partition. RANK() — ties get same rank, gaps after. DENSE_RANK() — ties same, no gaps. LAG(col, n) — value from n rows before. LEAD(col, n) — value from n rows ahead. SUM/AVG OVER — running total/average.
explainModes.standard: Window function syntax: func() OVER (PARTITION BY p ORDER BY o ROWS BETWEEN ... AND ...). Frame clause: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW (default for running sum). PARTITION BY is optional — omit to treat all rows as one window. Window functions run after WHERE/GROUP BY/HAVING, in the SELECT/ORDER BY phase. Cannot be used in WHERE or HAVING (use a CTE or subquery).
explainModes.technical: Frame types: ROWS (physical rows), RANGE (logical range of values — default for most functions). RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW groups ties together. FILTER clause works with window functions: SUM(col) FILTER (WHERE condition) OVER (...). Named windows: WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY ...) — reuse in multiple functions. Aggregate functions (SUM, AVG, COUNT) can all be used as window functions with OVER.
explainModes.deepDive: Window functions are computed in a single pass with the sort for ORDER BY — efficient. For large datasets, PARTITION BY reduces sort size. First/last value in a window: FIRST_VALUE(col) OVER (...) and LAST_VALUE with correct frame. Percentile: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col) — exact median in PostgreSQL. NTH_VALUE(col, n). CUME_DIST() — cumulative distribution. PERCENT_RANK(). The combination of CTE + window function is the most powerful pattern for analytical SQL.

content.code:
-- ROW_NUMBER: sequential numbers within partition
SELECT
    name, category, price,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS rank_in_category
FROM products;

-- RANK: ties get the same rank, with gaps
-- DENSE_RANK: ties get the same rank, no gaps
SELECT
    name, total,
    RANK()       OVER (ORDER BY total DESC) AS rank_with_gap,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total DESC) AS rank_no_gap
FROM orders;

-- Top product per category (using ROW_NUMBER)
-- (CTEs will be explained in the next lesson)
SELECT name, category, price
FROM (
    SELECT
        name, category, price,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS rn
    FROM products
)
WHERE rn = 1;

-- LAG: value from the previous row
-- LEAD: value from the next row
SELECT
    id, total, ordered_at,
    LAG(total)  OVER (ORDER BY ordered_at) AS prev_order_total,
    LEAD(total) OVER (ORDER BY ordered_at) AS next_order_total,
    total - LAG(total) OVER (ORDER BY ordered_at) AS change_from_prev
FROM orders;

-- Running total (cumulative sum)
SELECT
    ordered_at,
    total,
    SUM(total) OVER (ORDER BY ordered_at) AS running_total
FROM orders;

-- Running total per user
SELECT
    user_id,
    total,
    ordered_at,
    SUM(total) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ordered_at) AS user_running_total
FROM orders;

-- Average + count alongside individual rows
-- (without GROUP BY — rows are NOT collapsed)
SELECT
    name, price, category,
    ROUND(AVG(price) OVER (PARTITION BY category), 2) AS category_avg,
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY category) AS category_count
FROM products;

questions.question: What is the key difference between window functions and GROUP BY aggregation?
options: Window functions collapse multiple rows into one; GROUP BY doesn't
GROUP BY collapses rows; window functions compute aggregates without collapsing rows
questions.explanation: GROUP BY collapses multiple rows into one row per group — you lose the individual row details. Window functions add computed values (rank, running total, etc.) to EACH row without collapsing them. This lets you see individual order details AND their rank simultaneously.

faq.q: What is PARTITION BY in a window function?
faq.a: PARTITION BY divides rows into groups (like GROUP BY), but rows stay separate — they're not collapsed. The window function is computed independently for each partition. ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price) gives separate 1,2,3 numbering within each category.

examples: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY created_at) — number a user's orders
SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY month ORDER BY day) — cumulative monthly revenue
LAG(price) OVER (ORDER BY date) — compare today's price to yesterday
